# Visibility board

The performance board discipline pointed at a commercial function: bookings, pipeline quality, service velocity, team productivity — Plan vs. Actual, period by period, computed red or green from real numbers, closing the loop into a gemba-grounded root-cause log and a countermeasure register, and honestly telling a real sustained problem apart from a single isolated miss.

Family: Daily management · Format: .xlsx · Domain: commercial

## What it is

A visibility board is the performance board discipline pointed at a commercial function — bookings, pipeline quality, service velocity, team productivity — instead of a shop floor. Each KPI gets a real monthly plan and a computed status, never asserted, and a sustained problem (two or more consecutive red periods) is named separately from a single isolated miss, because reacting to both the same way burns root-cause effort chasing noise instead of a real trend. Gemba in a commercial workflow isn't the shop floor — it's the CRM quote queue, the order intake portal, the ERP contract master, the pricing approval inbox — and a real abnormality log entry comes from direct observation there, not speculation about what probably happened.

## When to use it

Use it when:

- A commercial function already has (or can name) the vital few KPIs that actually matter — bookings, quote quality, turnaround time, SLA compliance — and wants an honest, computed record of how each is tracking.
- You want a red period to trigger real root-cause work in the actual commercial systems (the CRM, the ERP, the pricing engine), not a status update nobody follows up on.
- You want to know honestly which misses are a real, sustained pattern worth escalating and which are a single blip that already recovered, before spending a review cycle on the wrong one.

Not when:

- You don't have a real plan or target for the KPI yet, just a hope it trends the right way — set a real plan first, or every period reads as an ungrounded pass/fail.
- You're tracking this KPI nowhere near its own review cadence — a board reviewed monthly needs monthly discipline behind it, not numbers nobody's actually checking.
- You're tempted to list every metric the CRM can report — the vital few discipline applies here too; a board with real ownership beats an exhaustive dashboard nobody discusses.

## How to fill it in

- **kpis** — Describe the commercial function and what matters to it — a first-pass KPI set gets drafted, each with a monthly plan. Enter actuals yourself as each period closes; a real reported number is never invented.
- **coverage** — Computed for you from your KPIs, once actuals are entered — nothing to enter here.
- **abnormalities** — Log one whenever a period comes in red — a real cause observed directly in the CRM quote queue, order intake, or wherever the work actually lives, not a guess.
- **countermeasures** — What will restore the standard, owned and dated — containment (protects delivery now) or permanent (fixes the root cause in the system or process).
- **narrative** — Drafted from the board actually built.

## What good looks like

The example below is Beacon Analytics' own commercial operations board — quote first-pass yield is a genuine three-month sustained miss (a first countermeasure closed on time but a second, unrelated failure mode kept it going), while commercial bookings had a single red month that recovered the next one and correctly doesn't get flagged the same way.

Full worked example, on-screen and as a downloadable .xlsx: https://katafacts.com/katas/visibility-board

## Common mistakes

- **Reacting to every red period identically, whether it's an isolated blip or a real trend.** — A single miss with no real pattern is usually ordinary variation — root-causing it wastes effort, and when a number drifts back to green on its own, a countermeasure often gets wrongly credited for a recovery that would have happened anyway.
- **Logging an abnormality's cause from a guess about the CRM or ERP instead of actually looking.** — A root cause written from speculation is usually wrong, and a fix built on the wrong root cause doesn't actually stop the recurrence — check the actual system before writing the cause down.
- **Treating a closed countermeasure as proof the KPI is fixed, without checking the KPI actually recovered.** — A countermeasure can close on schedule and still not hold — the honest signal is whether the KPI itself returns to green, not whether the action item got checked off.

## What it connects to

Upstream:

- **Sales funnel value stream map** — A flow-efficiency or conversion finding from the funnel VSM is exactly the kind of thing that turns into one of this board's own KPIs.
- **KPI tree** — A KPI tree's driver decomposition is what earns a metric its place on this board in the first place — this tracks it over time, the tree explains why it matters.

Downstream:

- **Pipeline management board** — This board's monthly review names what's off track; the daily/weekly tiered huddle cadence is where an abnormality actually gets worked between reviews.
- **Deal A3 — win-rate root cause analysis** — When a sustained-miss KPI's quick countermeasure doesn't hold, a deal A3 is where the root cause gets worked with the full discipline it deserves.

## Where AI helps

Judgement — stays with you:

- Deciding which commercial KPIs are actually the vital few worth tracking
- Deciding whether a miss is worth escalating now or watching another period

Analysis — AI helps:

- Drafting a first-pass KPI set and monthly plan from a description of the commercial function
- Drafting the narrative from the board actually built

Drudgery — automated:

- Computing red/green status per period and the plan-to-date vs. actual-to-date rollup
- Counting on-track, sustained-miss, and not-yet-reported KPIs
- Exporting to xlsx in the house format
